title: Candidate feedback draft: Aaron Brooks - Senior Serving Runtime Engineer
content:
Quick notes / draft for Aaron Brooks (onsite loop 2026-03-06) - Senior Serving Runtime Engineer

SUMMARY
- Overall impression: strong systems background with real GPU infra exposure. Confident, pragmatic. Would be an above-average IC for the serving-runtime team.
- Recommendation (initial): Hire / strong hire with an expectation-setting conversation about ownership of specific kernel-level work vs. infra orchestration.

RESUME HIGHLIGHTS
- 6+ years backend/C++/Python, last 3 years focused on model serving at startup (served BERT-like models in production).
- Open-source contributions: patches to memory allocator and a small attention-optimization repo (linked in resume).
- Past role included end-to-end ownership from model export to ops runbook - helpful for our Dedicated/Private product mix.

INTERVIEW BREAKDOWN (by interviewer notes)
1) System design (Samir Patel) - 7/10
  - Good decomposition for multi-tenant GPU serving: worker pools, routing, cache invalidation.
  - Brought up KV cache eviction tradeoffs and sticky routing, but didn't quantify memory/cpu cost for a 10k rps workload.
  - Follow-ups: ask for more concrete latency numbers and batch sizing rationale in a follow-up take-home.
2) Coding (Jordan Sanchez) - 8/10
  - Clean Python prototype for dynamic batching (pseudocode).
  - Edge-case handling solid (partial batch flush, timeouts).
  - Minor nit: used blocking sleep in sketch - would have used async/await + loop integration for production.
3) Performance/kernel knowledge (Priya Desai) - 7/10
  - Understands GPU memory fragmentation causes, fragmentation mitigation (defragmentation windows), and basic quantization tradeoffs.
  - Less familiarity with our custom fused-kernel approach (didn't know Triton heuristics we use) but showed quick learning curve.
4) Behavioral / culture (hiring mgr) - 9/10
  - Good ownership stories, prioritization of reliability over micro-optimizations, aligns with SRE-ish mindset.

STRENGTHS
- Strong ownership of infra + product sensitivity ties (understands cost vs latency tradeoffs)
- Practical engineer: prioritizes observability and runbooks
- Familiarity with optimizer-ish work (quantization, memory management) that maps to Redwood Optimize feature set

CONCERNS / RISKS
- Not deep in our exact kernel stack (Triton/fused kernels) - but seems trainable
- Could be more conservative on measuring vs assumptions (some design answers lacked explicit numbers)
- Senior level gap? Might start as Senior IC but need to check ability to lead cross-team projects (ask references)

SCORECARD (draft numeric) - translate to role rubric later
- System design: "7"
- Coding: "8"
- Performance & infra knowledge: "7"
- Ownership / culture fit: "9"
- Communication: "8"
- Overall (avg): "7.8"

RECOMMENDED ROLE FIT / HIRE LEVEL
- Senior Software Engineer (Serving/Runtime) - immediate contributor.
- Potential to scale to Staff in ~12-18 months with ownership of one major infra feature (e.g., kernel selection/compilation pipeline).

NEXT STEPS
- Collect reference from previous manager about cross-team influence and kernel/optimizer ownership (Jordan to own).
- Quick follow-up question doc for candidate (2-3 targeted questions about kernel tradeoffs + one small task to show how they'd measure batch sizing impact).
- Team interviewers to sign off by 2026-03-10. If green, extend offer with standard Senior template.

NOTES / TODO (scratchpad style)
- Draft follow-up questions: what metrics would you capture for a new batching algorithm? how would you design A/B for quantization rollout?
- Check candidate's Github PRs (link in resume) for C++ allocator changes - ask about test coverage and perf regression testing.
- Compensation band: likely within Senior band 3 (confirm with compensation).

ROUGH EMAIL PITCH (for hiring manager)
Hi [Hiring Manager],

Short take: Aaron is a pragmatic infra-oriented engineer with strong ownership and the right cost/latency mindset. He lacks direct experience with our fused-kernel stack but demonstrated the ability to learn and has adjacent experience that maps well to our Optimize and Dedicated products. Recommend moving forward to reference check and a short follow-up technical question.

- Priya

(END)
